summary: Cut the first-load code by loading policy detail only when needed, repaired four Back and deep-link cases, and corrected wording that changed technical meaning. No scores or scoring rules changed.

items.headline: Policy detail waits until it is needed
items.body: The first JavaScript load fell from 535,131 bytes to 345,966 bytes without raising the build limits. The 241,544-byte policy-detail file now loads when a reader opens a card or the Promises section. A generated summary keeps the 12 cards, 43 promise totals, headline scores, and grade-move display aligned with the canonical policy data.

items.headline: Back and deep links keep their place
items.body: The safeguards link now has a real browser-history entry. Back and Forward also work after a quick card-close and section change, an address-bar link change, or a card reload.

items.headline: Technical wording corrected
items.body: A follow-up review restored the timing of the five-year defence commitment, the published Defence grade rationale, and the intended meaning of durable, material, and full-time-equivalent measures. It also corrected two lines that had overstated what affordability and carbon evidence showed.

items.headline: Review decisions recorded
items.body: The July 19 review record separates accepted fixes from the Economic Policy wording decision and physical device checks that still need the editor. No grade, threshold, formula, weight, promise status, source stack, or dimension-model rule changed.

summary: Made the dashboard faster to open and easier to link. Later sections now load only when opened, fonts stay on this site, and policy cards work with Back, deep links, and Share. Review-driven wording fixes also landed. No scores changed.

items.headline: Smaller first load
items.body: The first page now loads about 534 KB of JavaScript instead of the previous 781 KB single chunk. The 211 KB Change Log and the Promises, Rubric, and About sections wait until a reader opens them. A build gate checks the entry graph and keeps those routes separate.

items.headline: Fonts stay on this site
items.body: DM Sans, DM Mono, and DM Serif Display are now served with the dashboard instead of through Google Fonts. The browser no longer needs that outside font request, and the build checks the asset paths.

items.headline: Policy cards have working URLs
items.body: Opening a policy card now puts its link in the address bar. Browser Back closes it, a direct link restores it, and Share uses the device share sheet with a clipboard fallback. Desktop Back also returns focus to the card that opened the detail.

items.headline: Deferred sections fail inside the page
items.body: If a later section cannot load, the dashboard shell stays available with a reload action instead of turning blank. Delayed Change Log links now wait for their target, and a section click made during drawer Back finishes at the requested destination.

items.headline: Review wording reconciled
items.body: Defence's why-not explanation now follows its existing five-point trade marker, Ethics explains why the general ETHI report is not a second case-specific finding, and the Rubric tab describes the ungraded tracker and whole-letter files consistently. Economic Policy now states its two-lever count conflict honestly and leaves the binding-rule decision in the editor queue.

items.headline: Release and governance records synchronized
items.body: The July 4 review record, source-family rollup, data-shape guidance, frozen app-shell record, and roadmap now match the release package. No grade, threshold, formula, weight, source-stack, promise-status, or dimension-model rule changed.

items.headline: Plainer wording on the policy cards
items.body: A readability pass changed 44 lines across nine policy cards, including Flagship Delivery, to use plainer and shorter sentences. A later review found that some lines changed technical or evidentiary meaning, and v5.156 corrected those cases.

summary: A legibility pass for first-time readers. The Rubric tab now opens with a plain-language summary of how scoring works, each graded area answers why not higher and why not lower, and a continuity plan is published. No scores changed.

items.headline: Plain scoring explainer opens the Rubric tab
items.body: The Rubric tab now starts with a short plain-language summary of how the scoring works: what gets graded, how the two headline scores are built, where judgment enters, and what would move a grade. The model-limits list moved up with it, so the limits come before the mechanics.

items.headline: Why-not lines extend to the 10 other graded areas
items.body: The why-not-higher and why-not-lower lines piloted on Affordability Response now appear on each of the 11 graded areas. Each line is written from that area’s own published thresholds, quotes nothing that is not already in its data, and the data validator rejects grade letters and urgency wording.

items.headline: Continuity plan published
items.body: A new governance doc names the single-editor risk the July outside review flagged. It records where the canonical state lives, what one monthly cycle requires, what happens if updates stop, what is and is not transferable to a successor, and the orderly wind-down option.

summary: Follow-through on two outside reviews: a why-not-higher, why-not-lower explainer piloted on Affordability, a promise-status bar on the scoreboard, honest theme icons, and a set of small keyboard and text fixes. No scores changed.

items.headline: Why not higher, why not lower
items.body: The opened Affordability Response card now answers the two questions a skeptical reader asks first: what the next band up would require that the evidence does not show, and what the band below would require that existing measures contradict. The lines are written by the editor, checked by the data validator, and sit right under the live grade band. If the pilot reads well it extends to the other files.

items.headline: Promise status at a glance
items.body: The Promises Delivered card now carries a small bar showing how the 43 tracked commitments split across statuses, in the same colors as the Promises tab. The counts are spelled out in words for screen readers. It reports the mix. It does not celebrate it.

items.headline: Theme icons match the mode
items.body: The theme button now shows a sun in light mode, a moon in dark mode, and a half circle when following your device. Before this, light mode showed a moon and the light and system icons were easy to confuse.

items.headline: Keyboard and text fixes
items.body: Sidebar links now show a clear focus ring for keyboard readers. Trigger set dates can no longer wrap mid-date. Card verdict lines cap at two lines and the next-check line at one, with full text inside the opened card. Poll links in the Approval table now name the pollster and field dates for screen readers.

items.headline: Probation wording cleanup
items.body: Flagship Delivery exited probation after the July retention check, but a few pre-exit wording leftovers were still in the live data. They now read as past tense. The grade, the combination rule, and the exit record are unchanged.

items.headline: Two outside reviews adjudicated
items.body: A deep methods review and a live app-feel review were checked claim by claim. Several findings were already fixed in earlier releases, the real ones landed in this release, and the rest are queued with reasons in the review adjudication record.

summary: Small trust and calm improvements: trigger dates now show when each grade condition was set, the Change Log opens on major items, returning readers get a quiet caught-up line, and the theme control gains a follow-your-device option. No scores changed.

items.headline: Trigger conditions show their set date
items.body: Every up and down trigger in an opened dimension now shows the date its condition was published. The point is checkable fairness: the rules that decide a grade move were written before the evidence they now judge, and the score-math panel says so in one line.

items.headline: Change Log opens on the major items
items.body: The Changes tab now shows the newest dozen entries with documentation and minor items folded behind a small expander per entry. An explicit button reveals earlier history. Nothing loads on scroll.

items.headline: A quiet caught-up line for returning readers
items.body: When nothing has changed in the grades since your last visit, the dashboard now says so once, with the next scheduled update date, instead of saying nothing. It stays on your device, has no buttons, and appears once per release.

items.headline: Theme can follow your device
items.body: The theme button now cycles light, dark, and system. System follows your device setting live, so the dashboard changes with it at sunset instead of trapping you in a one-time choice.

summary: Made the dashboard read more like an app: a desktop sidebar, one-line verdicts on cards, a next-check line per dimension, a since-your-last-visit note, and a calendar file for the next update. No scores changed.

items.headline: Desktop workspace sidebar
items.body: On wide screens the five sections now live in a fixed left sidebar with the version and next update date, and it stays visible while a dimension is open. Phones keep the bottom navigation, and mid-size screens keep the top tabs.

items.headline: One-line verdicts on cards
items.body: Each graded card now opens with a single plain sentence giving the verdict gist, written by the editor and checked by the data validator so it can never contain a letter grade or urgency wording. The full status paragraph still lives inside the opened card.

items.headline: Next check on every card
items.body: Each graded card now shows the next scheduled evidence check for that file, taken word for word from the existing trigger data. It names what gets checked, never how close a grade is to moving.

items.headline: Since-your-last-visit note
items.body: Returning readers see one quiet, dismissible line counting grade changes since the version they last saw. It works entirely on your device with a single browser storage entry. The last-seen marker stays on your device and is not sent anywhere, and the build checks enforce that.

items.headline: Calendar file for the next update
items.body: The footer now offers a small calendar file (.ics) for the next scheduled update, alongside RSS and the email signup. It sets no reminder alarm. Real push notifications were considered and rejected: on a static site they would require a third-party push service, which fails the privacy bar.

summary: Applied the July monthly factual refreshes, refreshed Approval Signal, and closed the Flagship probation check with no grade moves.

items.headline: July monthly data refresh
items.body: Affordability Response now reflects May 2026 food CPI at 4.3%. Immigration now reflects the Q1 2026 temporary-resident share at 6.18%. Housing Supply now reflects May 2026 CMHC starts plus the latest Build Canada Homes and Ontario DCRP execution context. Major Projects now notes the June 24 Building Canada Act listing-process launch. All four files hold their grades.

items.headline: Approval Signal refreshed
items.body: Approval Signal now includes the latest Abacus and Leger approval waves plus June 19 and June 26 Nanos preferred-PM context. Research Co.'s June tariff-handling pair was reviewed but kept out because it does not match the broad PM/government job-approval construct used by the included pollsters.

items.headline: Flagship probation exit
items.body: Flagship Delivery passed its first full monthly retention check, so the probation label and July-only expiry language were removed from the live data and methodology docs. This was a rules cleanup only, not a grade move.

items.headline: Every cited source re-checked
items.body: The July cycle re-checked all 153 cited source links across every surface that carries one: source lists, trigger evidence and challenge sources, metric references, project and promise links, and Approval Signal polls. Each publisher site was also searched for June releases, with negative results logged rather than skipped. Every live cited link resolved. A new build check now blocks a monthly cycle from closing while any cited link is missing from the coverage ledger or any row is left unchecked.

items.headline: Separate v5.150 monthly-cycle release
items.body: Cut the July monthly cycle as v5.150 instead of folding it into the unpublished v5.149 UI draft. Coverage now runs through June 30, 2026, the next scheduled cycle moves to August 1, 2026, and history records the unchanged July score snapshot.

summary: Added a visible full-changelog link after the live coverage audit found older history was not reachable from the Changes tab.

items.headline: Full changelog link
items.body: The Changes tab now links to the full changelog file on GitHub so readers can reach older update history from the live dashboard. No grades, thresholds, formulas, source data, promise statuses, or methodology rules changed.

summary: Made the score weighting caveat and two methodology cleanup items visible without changing any grades.

items.headline: Composite score caveat and affordability inspectability
items.body: The Household Impact and Full Policy Audit cards now say that their averages depend on weighting choices and point readers to the score math below. Affordability Response also now shows a bounded why-not-higher and why-not-lower explanation inside the drawer. No grades, thresholds, or GPA formulas changed.

items.headline: Defence and Flagship rules reconciled
items.body: Defence & Trade now uses one canonical split-tripwire across the live data and methodology docs: opposite sub-score movement or a gap above 1.0 GPA points for two consecutive monthly review cycles queues the split. Flagship Delivery's probation now has an explicit July 2026 exit test instead of open-ended rollover.

items.headline: Review follow-through docs added
items.body: Added a practical Comet execution list and a continuity quickstart so the June 30 review stack turns into an actionable work queue instead of living only in pasted notes.

summary: Fixed the header badge spacing across desktop and mobile.

items.headline: Header badge spacing fix
items.body: The Performance Dashboard badge now sits below the theme button on all screen sizes, not just phones, and the browser smoke test checks the badge geometry so the collision cannot slip through again. Scores, grades, thresholds, source data, and evidence wording are unchanged.

summary: Fixed the mobile header badge layout after the civic identity pass.

items.headline: Mobile header badge fix
items.body: The Performance Dashboard badge now reserves space for its accent dots and sits below the theme button on phones, so the badge text no longer overlaps or wraps awkwardly. Scores, grades, thresholds, source data, and evidence wording are unchanged.

summary: Fixed the mobile dimension drawer containment after the identity pass.

items.headline: Mobile drawer containment fix
items.body: Mobile dimension drawers now drop the app-shell route-transition transform while open, so the drawer stays tied to the viewport instead of inheriting the height of the scorecard page. Scores, grades, thresholds, source data, routes, and evidence wording are unchanged.

summary: Gave the app shell a calmer civic identity pass without changing any scores.

items.headline: Civic identity polish
items.body: The header, score cards, status card, dimension cards, and mobile bottom navigation now use a more distinctive editorial Canada treatment: forest ink, quiet maple-red accents, warmer paper surfaces, and softer depth. The evidence path, routes, scores, grades, thresholds, and source data are unchanged.

summary: Added a sourced grade-move evidence loop without changing any scores.

items.headline: Grade moves tied to changelog evidence
items.body: The dashboard status card now reports grade moves for the current release, and dimension cards can show a calm grade-move marker only when the latest changelog entry has a matching grade item. This release has no grade move, so the marker renders empty by design.

items.headline: Change markers guarded by data checks
items.body: The data validator now checks current-release grade moves against the dimension's current grade, previous grade, dimension name, drivers, and evidence link. The browser smoke checks that card markers match the current changelog and that no personalized visit tracking was added.

summary: Retired the classic rollback route and moved the browser smoke into Pages CI.

items.headline: App shell as the only public route
items.body: The root and old ?experience=classic links now open the app shell after the clean June 29 route-exit audit. The completed classic-route check was removed from the public next-checks strip. No grades, thresholds, source data, promise statuses, or scoring rules changed.

items.headline: Browser smoke in Pages CI
items.body: The GitHub Pages workflow now runs the Playwright browser smoke before deploy. The job covers navigation, Major Projects source deep links, console errors, overflow, reduced motion, and stale classic links.

summary: Added a data-driven next-checks strip and a manual browser smoke test for the app shell.

items.headline: Next checks in dashboard status
items.body: The dashboard status card now shows the next evidence checks from status metadata: Housing disbursement, the classic-route exit, and the July monthly cycle. The validator checks the new schema and blocks urgency language or personalized watch-item fields.

items.headline: Manual browser smoke harness
items.body: Added a Playwright browser smoke test that covers root and classic routes, desktop and mobile widths, the five dashboard destinations, Major Projects source deep links, console errors, overflow, and reduced motion. It is a manual gate for one stable release before any CI promotion.

summary: Finished the plain-language pass across the non-dimension dashboard surfaces.

items.headline: Plain-language dashboard surfaces
items.body: The headline score cards, score-math panels, Approval Signal, Rubric tab, and About tab now use plainer wording for policy areas, grade-move conditions, source checks, polling averages, and score explanations. No grades, thresholds, source data, GPA formulas, or methodology rules changed.

summary: Tightened the plain-language wording in dimension details without changing any scores.

items.headline: Plain-language dimension detail pass
items.body: Dimension detail copy now uses plainer labels for the tracker pill, source freshness, project-list progress, scoring adjustments, and grade limits. Major Projects and Defence & Trade carry the calibration standard for the pass, and the same wording cleanup was scaled across the remaining dimension detail copy. No grades, thresholds, dates, source URLs, source counts, or GPA formulas changed.

items.headline: Calibration record
items.body: Added a short calibration pack that maps the rendered drawer order and records the Major Projects and Defence & Trade meaning-preservation checks used for the plain-language pass.

summary: Added a source freshness cue to the dimension detail drawer.

items.headline: Source freshness in dimension detail
items.body: The Sources affordance now shows the newest dated source before a reader opens the full source table, and the Sources section explains that the table is newest-first. This keeps count, freshness, and citation access together. No scores changed.

summary: Tightened the dimension detail drawer so grade movement and sources sit before longer rationale sections.

items.headline: Dimension detail reading order
items.body: The dimension drawer now exposes grade movement from the evidence snapshot and orders the detail path as verdict, evidence, triggers, sources, then rationale and criteria. Existing anchors and drawer controls stay in place. No scores changed.

summary: Added a quiet dashboard status card that separates source checking from editor-reviewed score cycles.

items.headline: Dashboard status card
items.body: A new card below the headline score row shows the latest evidence scan, the next scheduled scan, the editor-reviewed score cycle, coverage date, and monitor items awaiting review. It keeps source freshness separate from score review so the dashboard does not read like a live feed.

items.headline: Status metadata guardrails
items.body: The status card now reads from src/data/status.json, with a prebuild validator that checks date alignment, schedule direction, the coverage date, and blocked urgency language. No grade, threshold, GPA formula, source stack, or dimension-model change is part of this release.

summary: Added a dark theme with a header toggle, and recolored the top label so it no longer matches the failing-grade red.

items.headline: Dark mode
items.body: There is now a dark theme. A sun and moon button in the top-left of the header switches it, your choice is remembered, and it follows your device setting by default. Each view was set up so text stays readable on the dark background. Grades keep their red-to-green colors as bright chips so they still read at a glance, and the dark-theme rules leave the existing light-theme colors alone.

items.headline: Header label recolored
items.body: The 'Performance Dashboard' label at the top used the same red as a failing grade, which could read as a signal. It is now a neutral amber so it does not look like a score.

items.headline: Color and spacing tokens tidied
items.body: The two near-identical blues used for links and focus rings were merged into one, and some gaps were moved onto the shared spacing scale. No visible change in light mode.

summary: Visual refresh so the dashboard reads more like an app: cards lift off the page, the close button is a standard icon control, and controls give a small press response. No scores changed.

items.headline: Cards lift off the page
items.body: Every card now sits on a soft shadow against the background instead of a flat hairline box, so the layout reads as layered surfaces. Corner rounding is consistent across all cards now. A new set of surface and shadow tokens drives this, and also lays the groundwork for a dark mode.

items.headline: Standard close button on opened dimensions
items.body: The opened-dimension close button changed from a solid dark Close pill to a standard top-right icon button. On desktop it is an X in a quiet rounded chip with a Close label. On mobile it is a 44px icon-only circle. It keeps the easy-to-find treatment from the last update without looking like a heavy main action.

items.headline: Controls respond to taps
items.body: Cards, the tab bar, the mobile bottom nav, and the section toggles now give a small, fast press and hover response, so the interface feels touchable. All of it is turned off for readers who prefer reduced motion.

items.headline: Smoother opening, and the close stays put
items.body: Opening a dimension now fades in instead of snapping. On desktop, the section tabs step aside while a dimension is open, so the title and Close button stay pinned at the top instead of sliding behind the tab bar when you scroll. On phones the open animation is a touch quicker. Reduced-motion settings are respected.

summary: Corrected a stale industrial carbon price figure to match the May 2026 benchmark update.

items.headline: Industrial carbon price corrected to $95 (2026)
items.body: The Carbon Pricing rationale and a critics note still cited the old $110/tonne 2026 headline. The federal benchmark was updated on May 15, 2026 to $95/tonne for 2026 (per Canada.ca, matching the dimension's own metric). Both now read $95. The grade is unchanged, since it scores the effective market price, not the headline figure.

summary: Made the close button on an opened dimension easier to spot.

items.headline: Clearer close button on opened dimensions
items.body: On desktop, the close button on an opened dimension was a faint outline that was easy to miss. It is now a solid dark button, so it is obvious how to close the card. Mobile matches.

summary: Rewrote the dimension drawers and explainer copy so the grading logic is easier to follow without changing the scores.

items.headline: Plainer dashboard explanations
items.body: The policy drawers, score-math panels, About page, and Methodology page now explain more of the grading logic in plain language, especially acronyms, fiscal anchors, delivery status, and terms like material or binding delivery. The pass keeps the same grades, numbers, thresholds, source links, and trigger rules.

items.headline: Precision guardrails kept
items.body: The rewrite kept protected terms where they carry scoring meaning and added short glosses instead of swapping them for looser words. No grade, formula, weight, promise status, or dimension-model change is part of this release.

summary: Added a one-line note under the title explaining what "Canada Under Carney" means, after a reader read it as loaded.

items.headline: Title clarifier on the first screen
items.body: A reader heard "Canada Under Carney" as a loaded phrase. A new line under the title now says it is a time-period label, like "Canada under Chrétien" or "Canada under Diefenbaker," and that the scorecard grades the Carney government's performance, not Canada itself.

items.headline: Header tidy-up and plainer wording
items.body: Moved the one-line summary above the trust frame, trimmed a duplicate sentence, and replaced the jargon word "rule" with plainer wording. Display only, no grade or data change.

summary: The Promises summary card at the top now opens the Promises tab when you click it.

items.headline: Promises card is now clickable
items.body: The Promises Delivered card in the top row was the only summary card that did nothing when clicked. It now opens the full Promises tab, with a 'See all promises' cue so it's clear you can.

summary: Made the signup clearer about the confirmation email and where to find it if it lands in spam.

items.headline: Spam-folder heads-up at signup
items.body: The monthly-updates box now says you'll get a confirmation email to opt in, with a bolded reminder to check your spam folder if it's not in your inbox.

items.headline: Confirmation email names the dashboard
items.body: The opt-in email now says Canada Under Carney in the subject and explains what you signed up for, instead of a generic confirmation.

summary: Fixed the email signup, which had stopped accepting subscribers, by moving it from Buttondown to Kit.

items.headline: Email signup works again
items.body: The subscribe form had been failing (the old provider's free tier was full). It now posts to Kit with double opt-in, so you get a confirmation email before anything is sent. Same card, same consent checkbox, no third-party script added.

items.headline: Funding note updated
items.body: The About page now reflects that email distribution runs on Kit's free tier.

summary: Adjusted a few drawer-only type sizes so the opened dimension view reads more evenly.

items.headline: Opened-dimension type polish
items.body: Reduced the headline target/result value size, brought the headline label up to the evidence-label size, and raised the smallest source micro-labels from 10px to 11px. The change is limited to opened-dimension drawer typography.

items.headline: Scores unchanged
items.body: Display only. No promise status, grade, policy data, scoring rule, threshold, formula, weight, GPA, or dimension model changed.

summary: Added status evidence for the Foreign Policy Review promise while keeping it Too Early.

items.headline: Foreign Policy Review status evidence added
items.body: Added a Canadian Press report carrying Minister Anand's sequencing statement: the national-security strategy comes first, then Global Affairs launches the foreign-policy review. That supports the current Too Early status because no formal launch, terms of reference, or scope has been published.

items.headline: One status-link gap remains
items.body: Promise Tracker status-evidence coverage is now 42 of 43. The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism remains blank because the checked ECCC source is about EU and UK CBAM engagement, not Canada's own mechanism.

items.headline: Scores unchanged
items.body: Status evidence only. No promise status, grade, scoring rule, threshold, formula, weight, GPA, or dimension model changed.

summary: Updated the Red Tape Review promise after official progress reports became available.

items.headline: Red Tape Review promise moved to In Progress
items.body: Treasury Board now has an official Red Tape Review Progress Report, with department-level reports such as Transport Canada's showing completed, in-progress, and longer-term actions. The promise moved from Too Early to In Progress because reports are public, but the evidence still points to a regulatory pipeline rather than a completed result.

items.headline: Status evidence link added
items.body: Added the Treasury Board progress report as the promise's status-evidence source. Foreign Policy Review and the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism remain without status-evidence links because no clean official launch or framework document surfaced in this pass.

items.headline: Scores unchanged
items.body: Promise status and evidence only. No grade, scoring rule, threshold, formula, weight, GPA, or dimension model changed.

summary: Opening a dimension's promises now filters the Promises tab to that dimension, and corrected the housing 500,000-homes promise text and its source to match the platform.

items.headline: Promises open filtered to the dimension
items.body: From a dimension, tapping tracked promises and then Open the Promises tab now lands on the Promises view pre-filtered to that dimension, instead of the full list. The Promises nav tab still shows everything.

items.headline: Housing promise text and source corrected
items.body: Changed the housing target promise to 'Almost 500,000 new homes a year' to match the Liberal housing plan wording, and pointed its source to the page that carries that figure. The old text added a 'next decade' framing the cited source did not contain.

items.headline: Scores unchanged
items.body: Display and data labelling only. No grade, scoring rule, threshold, formula, weight, GPA, promise status, or dimension model changed.

summary: Added a headline commitment row to the dimension view that shows a stated target next to the externally reported result, starting with Defence and the NATO 2% target.

items.headline: Headline commitment: target vs result
items.body: The evidence snapshot can now lead with a stated commitment and the measured result side by side. Defence shows the NATO 2% of GDP target against Canada's 2.01% (2025 estimate), with both sources one tap away. It reads as accountability, not the grade.

items.headline: Comparison is derived, not typed
items.body: The target and result are formatted from their numeric values, and the comparison word is computed from them and checked by a build test, so what you read cannot drift from the data.

items.headline: Defence NATO 2% promise reworded
items.body: Changed the promise text from 'Exceed NATO 2% before 2030' to 'Meet NATO 2% (achieved 2025)'. The government's own wording is meet, and the 2% was reached in 2025, so the old before-2030 framing was stale.

items.headline: Scores unchanged
items.body: Display only. No grade, scoring rule, threshold, formula, weight, GPA, or dimension model changed. The new comparison is not a scored input.

summary: Reworked the opened-dimension view so the evidence that drives each grade leads, with the long-form reasoning moved into a check-this-grade layer.

items.headline: Evidence leads the dimension view
items.body: Opening a dimension now shows the grade once, then an evidence snapshot of headline metrics, sources, and promises tracked, with the verdict and full reasoning a tap below.

items.headline: Reasoning moved to a check-this-grade layer
items.body: Why this grade, the scoring rule and thresholds, triggers, perspectives, and scope notes are now disclosure sections you open to check the read or go deeper, instead of a wall of text on open.

items.headline: Headline metrics are editor-selected
items.body: Each graded dimension marks a few headline metrics for the evidence snapshot. These are a display choice, not a weighted input. The full metric list stays one tap away and unchanged.

items.headline: Scores and data unchanged
items.body: Presentation and navigation only. No grade, scoring rule, policy data, promise status, threshold, formula, weight, or dimension model changed.

summary: Polished post-cutover navigation and fixed state handling when the viewport changes.

items.headline: Mobile navigation icons added
items.body: The bottom navigation now pairs each label with a distinct icon, making the main destinations easier to scan on a phone.

items.headline: Active filters offer a return path
items.body: When promise filters are active, the result state now includes a direct way back to the filter controls instead of leaving readers to find them again.

items.headline: Bottom navigation re-entry motion
items.body: The mobile bottom navigation now uses a short re-entry motion when it returns, with reduced-motion preferences still respected.

items.headline: Semantic navigation retained
items.body: The primary views remain semantic navigation with buttons and aria-current. An APG tab widget was considered and rejected because these destinations behave as navigation, not one tab-panel set.

items.headline: Viewport state repaired
items.body: Switching between mobile and desktop widths now clears stale body locking and keeps navigation history aligned with the visible view.

items.headline: Scores and policy data unchanged
items.body: This release changes presentation, navigation, and viewport state handling only. No grade, scoring rule, policy data, promise status, threshold, formula, weight, or dimension model changed.

summary: Made the app shell the default dashboard after closing the desktop and mobile focus blockers.

items.headline: App shell at the root
items.body: The root now opens the app shell. Add ?experience=classic to use the previous dashboard during this release if a rollback is needed.

items.headline: Keyboard focus blockers closed
items.body: Desktop detail now receives keyboard focus and closes with Escape. Closing returns focus to the card that opened it. On mobile, Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside the open drawer, with Escape and focus return preserved.

items.headline: Scores and evidence unchanged
items.body: This release changes the default presentation and focus behavior only. Grades, scoring rules, policy data, approval data, promise statuses, thresholds, formulas, weights, and the 11-plus-1 dimension model are unchanged.

summary: Added an optional public app-shell beta while keeping the classic dashboard as the default.

items.headline: Public app-shell beta
items.body: The app-style dashboard can now be opened with ?experience=app. The root and ?experience=classic continue to open the classic dashboard during the beta.

items.headline: Production evidence retained
items.body: The beta reuses the production dimension detail, score derivations, Approval drilldown, Change Log, Methodology, and About surfaces instead of maintaining reduced copies.

items.headline: Scoring boundary unchanged
items.body: This release changes presentation and navigation only. No grade, threshold, formula, weight, promise status, approval data, or dimension model changed.

items.body: Open cards now lead with a verdict, a merged why block, and an at-a-glance panel with triggers and top metrics. Desktop section navigation now uses Verdict, Why, Triggers or Moves, Sources, and Rule, while mobile keeps the shorter action set.

items.body: The June source-monitor candidates were opened and sorted. summary: Corrected the Approval Signal headline: reverted the house-effect de-housing that was pushing the number above every input poll. Approve/disapprove now read 58/30 (was 61/34), inside the range of the actual polls.

items.headline: Reverted the polling house-effect correction
items.body: The v5.92 house-effect de-housing over-corrected with only three firms in the window: it lifted every Abacus poll by about 4.3 points and, since Abacus was three of the five polls, drove the aggregate to 61% approve — higher than the highest input poll (59%). A weighted average cannot legitimately exceed all of its inputs, so de-housing was pulled. The headline is now a plain sample-and-recency-weighted mean of the raw polls: 58% approve / 30% disapprove, net +28, inside the 54-59% range of the actual polls. Recency decay (30-day half-life) is kept. The underlying poll data is accurate (the 59/27 Abacus entry matches the May 24 Abacus release verbatim). De-housing can return later, centred and with broader firm coverage. Method: docs/Polling-Aggregation-Method-2026-06.md.

On a grade change, a reviewer holding a different political prior independently checks whether the same evidence yields the same grade, externalizing the party-symmetry test the editor currently applies alone. It flags rather than changes grades, stays separate from the inter-rater reliability pilot (which screens political agreement out by design), and complements the reader-facing perceived-bias survey. items.headline: Approval polling: recency decay + house-effect correction
items.body: The Approval Signal aggregate now weights each poll by recency (30-day half-life) on top of sample size, and subtracts each firm's house effect (its standing lean versus other firms polling the same weeks, leave-one-pollster-out, for firms with at least 3 polls). On the current window this moves the headline from 57/30 (net +27) to 61/34 (net +26): approve and disapprove each rise about 4 points because the window is Abacus-heavy and Abacus runs low on both. The per-firm offsets are shown in the drill-down. The signal is ungraded, so the GPA math is untouched. Method: docs/Polling-Aggregation-Method-2026-06.md.

All now state one canonical rule: if the defence and trade sub-scores move in opposite directions, or diverge by more than 1.0 GPA points (about one full letter grade), for two consecutive review cycles, the split shadow promotes. summary: Absorbed three skills from Matt Pocock's skills repo (grill-me, review, write-a-skill), adapted to this project, and added two git safety nets: a pre-commit hook (blocks absolute-path leaks, runs test:data) and a git-guardrails Claude Code hook (blocks destructive git commands). No dashboard data or grade impact.

items.headline: grill-me, review, write-a-skill skills added
items.body: After reviewing the full Matt Pocock skills repo, absorbed the three that fit a data/methodology project (skipped the GitHub-issue/PRD-dependent and coding-specific ones). grill-me: one-question-at-a-time interrogation of an editor decision, routed through grade-evaluation (no autonomous grade moves). review: two-axis Standards-vs-Spec diff review via parallel sub-agents — an in-house second opinion when Codex/Comet are unavailable. write-a-skill: encodes the house format and the under-100-lines / triggers-in-description / identifier-scan conventions so the skill set stays consistent. All three built Carney-local plus global Claude and Codex versions.

items.headline: Pre-commit hook (identity-neutral)
items.body: scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit blocks staged absolute local paths (the v5.72 leak class), runs git diff --cached --check, and runs test:data when src/data is staged. Identity-neutral by design — the committed hook contains no names; editor-identity patterns live in a gitignored .identity-patterns file read at runtime. Install with npm run setup:hooks. Verified: blocks a /Users/ leak, passes clean content, and does not false-positive on skill files that document the scan regex.

items.headline: git-guardrails hook blocks destructive git
items.body: scripts/git-hooks/block-dangerous-git.sh, wired as a PreToolUse Bash hook in .claude/settings.json, blocks the agent from running force push, reset --hard, clean -f, branch -D, push --delete / push :ref, filter-branch, update-ref -d, and reflog expire --expire=now. Allows --force-with-lease and all normal add/commit/push/status/log/diff/checkout. Dependency-free POSIX sh, identity-neutral. Pipe-tested: 9/9 destructive blocked, 9/9 normal allowed. Activates after opening /hooks once or restarting (the project settings.json is new this session).

items.headline: .gitignore: .identity-patterns

items.body: Comet's review of the v5.65 commit and the bundled audit-script source flagged that scripts/audit-bias-resistance.mjs collectAllSources() and collectGradeMovingSources() did not read gradeTriggers.up/down[].additionalSources[]. The v5.65 changelog claim that 'bias-audit count holds at 6 baseline' was honest against what the script then measured, but the script wasn't measuring the v5.64 threading layer the dashboard already renders to readers. Both collectors now include trigger.additionalSources[] entries with explicit origin tags ('trigger.up.additionalSources' / 'trigger.down.additionalSources'). After the fix: total flagged dimensions still 6 (same baseline), but per-dimension family distributions for Economic Policy Response, Affordability Response, and Immigration now correctly reflect the v5.64 threading. Family 7 (Policy institute) grade-moving counts went up in Immigration from 1 to 4, in Economic Policy from 0 to 2, and in Affordability the family-9 grade-moving count rose from 3 to 5 — same dimensions, fuller picture of independent-challenge evidence. The 6 still-flagged dimensions are flagged for trigger asymmetry (carbon-pricing, immigration, ethics-transparency), numeric-threshold asymmetry (immigration, housing-supply, promise-delivery), press-release-in-chain (housing-supply), or 80% policy-institute concentration (execution-delivery) — all unrelated to family classification of additionalSources. No data changes. No grade changes. No threshold changes. No GPA formula changes.

items.body: Climate trim: removed CCI industrial pricing gaps (the broader CCI off-course publication is retained as the primary 2030-target source); removed ECCC 2024-25 departmental plan (the newer 2025-26 plan is retained). Housing additions: CHBA Q1 2026 Housing Market Index (https://www.chba.ca/2026/04/21/low-builder-confidence-illustrates-need-for-sustained-federal-action-plan-focused-on-homeownership-housing/) threaded into the Housing starts (Mar 2026 trend / SAAR) metric — CHBA provides supply-side builder-confidence ground truth that cross-checks the CMHC trend reading; Scotiabank Economics Canadian Home Sales (Housing News Flash Feb 2026, https://www.scotiabank.com/ca/en/about/economics/economics-publications/post.other-publications.housing.housing-news-flash.february-18--2026.html) threaded into the same metric — adds the market-side independent voice on sales conditions feeding through to starts. SKIPPED for source-band ceiling (not URL availability): Pembina Institute (Climate already at 10 after trim+adds), Business Council of Canada (Economic Policy already at 10), Smart Prosperity Institute and National Bank (Housing already at 10 after CHBA+Scotiabank). Source M Democracy Watch and Source O Parliamentary ETHI Committee were already present in sources[] from prior commits; the new work was threading them into the governance-review metric with explicit role descriptions. Source N Transparency International Canada is a new pool addition. Bias-audit count: before (per docs/Source-To-Trigger-Followup-2026-05-23.md) was 6; after = 6 — same baseline maintained. The intermediate count of 9 during the work was caused entirely by audit-script taxonomy gaps (csls.ca, conferenceboard.ca, cer-rec.gc.ca, chba.ca, scotiabank.com/economics, maytree.com, transparencycanada.ca, foodbankscanada.ca were not yet in the source-family classifier); the audit script was extended to recognize these established Canadian source families in scripts/audit-bias-resistance.mjs (CER added to family 4; Conference Board, Maytree, Food Banks Canada, Smart Prosperity, Business Council added to family 7; CSLS and Scotiabank Economics and National Bank Economics added to family 9; Transparency International Canada added to family 10; CHBA added to family 11) — same precedent as v5.61 family-11 industry-association extension. The dashboard's source schema does not currently carry a per-source family field at the JSON level; the bias-audit script infers family from URL patterns. The Parliamentary ETHI Committee Report sourceRef under the Committee / governance review metric carries a role description noting it as family-6 parliamentary critique distinct from family-5 procedural. The six dimensions still flagged after this commit (carbon-pricing trigger asymmetry, immigration trigger asymmetry and numeric asymmetry, housing-supply press release in chain and numeric asymmetry, ethics-transparency down-trigger asymmetry, execution-delivery 80% policy-institute concentration, promise-delivery numeric asymmetry) are pre-existing methodology findings unrelated to the source-additions arc. The first single-model probe (Grok, 2026-05-17) surfaced two real findings for the June 2026 cycle (editor disclosure surface, version archive visibility) plus one methodology gap (the confabulation pattern that drove the verbatim-quote rule). items.headline: Inline text colors aligned to WCAG AA tokens

items.body: The 18 inter-rater packet source links were checked before recruitment. One broken House ETHI PDF link was replaced with the working House DocumentViewer report page in both the pilot packet and the live Ethics source list.

summary: May grade review: Fiscal Health moved up to C, Major Projects denominator was reconciled to the official MPO list, and Housing Supply kept D after the March starts check.

items.headline: Fiscal Health moved D → C
items.body: The Spring Economic Update lowered the projected FY 2025-26 deficit to $66.9B, and PBO now says both fiscal anchors are on track. The file stops at C because the deficit remains above the B threshold and PBO still flags capital-budgeting, interest-burden, and defence-cost caveats.
drivers: PBO says the deficit-to-GDP anchor is on track, declining from 2.1% in 2025-26 to 1.4% by 2030-31
PBO says the operating-balance anchor is projected to be met by 2028-29
Caveats remain on capital-budgeting definitions, rising interest burden, and omitted anticipated defence spending

items.headline: Fiscal-anchor promise moved back into progress
items.body: The operational-budget-balance promise now reads In Progress rather than Stalled. The evidence is still caveated: PBO says the anchors are on track, but also says the capital/operating classification needs more detail.

items.headline: Major Projects cohort denominator corrected to 15 projects
items.body: The official MPO page lists 15 referred projects and separates out transformative strategies. The dashboard now counts only the 15 projects in the cohort denominator; documented post-designation advancement remains 2 of 15, so the grade holds at C.

items.headline: Housing starts trigger reviewed and held
items.body: CMHC March 2026 starts showed a 235,852 monthly SAAR but a 248,378 six-month trend. Because CMHC says the trend measure smooths volatile monthly readings, the dashboard does not treat the one-month dip as firing the <240K down trigger while the trend remains above 240K.

summary: May source refresh: approval polling and several source metrics updated without changing grades.

items.headline: Approval Signal refreshed
items.body: Four recent approval polls from Abacus Data, Leger, and Angus Reid Institute were added. The 60-day sample-size-weighted display still rounds to 57% approve and 31% disapprove, net +26.

items.headline: Fiscal and labour metrics refreshed
items.body: Fiscal Health now uses the Spring Economic Update's $66.9B FY 2025-26 deficit projection and PBO's assessment that new measures offset most later fiscal room. Economic Policy now references the April Labour Force Survey.

items.headline: Affordability CPI refreshed
items.body: Affordability Response now uses March 2026 food-store CPI at 4.4% year over year. April CPI is scheduled for release on May 19.

items.headline: Manual review queue logged
items.body: The targeted source refresh flagged two calls for the grade-review phase: reconciling the Major Projects public project list with the live cohort, and deciding how the Housing Supply starts trigger should treat March CMHC starts data.

summary: Mobile evidence polish: the Major Projects full project list now uses readable project cards on phones.

items.headline: Major Projects list no longer needs sideways scrolling on mobile
items.body: The full project pipeline still uses the compact table on desktop, but phone-width screens now show stacked project cards with tranche, stage date, and source link visible in each card. No grades, scores, thresholds, source data, or methodology changed. The cohort denominator was later reconciled to 15 on 2026-05-13.

summary: Mobile card-spacing polish: dimension cards now have a little more breathing room while scrolling on phones.

items.headline: Scorecard cards breathe more on mobile
items.body: The mobile scorecard and tracker grids now use a wider gap between cards, responding to Reddit feedback that the grade cards felt cramped while scrolling. No grades, scores, sources, promise statuses, or methodology changed.

summary: Traceability polish: event-driven trigger sources now say so directly in the scoring drawer.

items.headline: Non-clickable trigger sources now identify event-driven evidence
items.body: Six grade-move triggers that depend on future events now label their source line as event-driven, so readers can distinguish evidence that already has a one-click source from evidence that would only exist if the trigger fires. No grades, scores, thresholds, source lists, or promise statuses changed.

summary: Scoring-boundary disclosure: the About and Methodology pages now state what the dashboard can and cannot score.

items.headline: About page now names the dashboard's scoring boundary
items.body: A new section explains that the dashboard scores sourceable federal action, documented commitments, published thresholds, and observable outcomes, not leadership style, symbolic politics, popularity, forecasts, or valuable outcomes that lack enough public evidence to grade.

items.headline: Methodology limits now address measurable-vs-valuable risk
items.body: The rubric limits now say plainly that the model can only score what can be inspected through public evidence, rather than estimating weakly evidenced qualities by proxy.

items.headline: README feature list reconciled with the live app
items.body: The removed Print / Export PDF feature is no longer advertised, and the About feature now mentions the new scoring-boundary disclosure.

summary: Mobile UX bug-fix bundle: trust frame is now global, evidence chips no longer clip on phones, drill-downs return readers to the scoreboard on close, and the project pipeline gives a clear scroll cue.

items.headline: What this is / what this isn't moved into the global header
items.body: The scope frame previously lived inside the Scorecard tab only. It now sits between the dashboard title and the scoreboard, so a reader who lands on Promises, Change Log, or Rubric still sees what the dashboard is and is not for.

items.headline: Print / Export PDF button removed
items.body: The button printed a screen-style page that was not optimized for paper. Removed alongside its print stylesheet rather than left as an unfulfilled promise.

items.headline: Promise tab evidence links no longer clip on mobile
items.body: Source and Status evidence chips on expanded promise rows now wrap their text instead of forcing a single line, so long source labels stay fully visible on narrow screens.

items.headline: Promise rows show a stronger details affordance
items.body: The previous pale chevron next to each promise now reads as a darker '▸ Details' / '▾ Hide' label so it is obvious that rows expand for evidence.

items.headline: Project pipeline now signals horizontal scroll
items.body: The Major Projects pipeline table now carries a 'Scroll right for stage date and source links →' caption and a right-edge fade gradient on narrow screens, so readers do not miss the source column.

items.headline: Tab rail signals overflow on narrow phones
items.body: On phones where 'Scorecard / Promises / Change Log / Rubric / About' overflows the rail, a small fade gradient on the right edge cues that more tabs sit off-screen.

items.headline: Closing a drill-down scrolls back to the scoreboard
items.body: On phones, hiding the score-derivation panel or the approval-signal drill-down now scrolls the page back to the scoreboard so readers do not have to manually backtrack.

items.headline: Evidence-link styling unified
items.body: Trigger-level evidence links and the project pipeline source column are now consistently rendered as 12px bold blue links, while file-level source chips remain the larger filled-chip treatment. Two visual treatments instead of five.

items.headline: Approval Signal card shares the same footer slot as the grade cards
items.body: 'See polls & sources' moved from the body of the Approval card into the footer slot, so all four scoreboard cards land their action affordance at the same vertical position.

items.headline: Trend arrows are now accessible
items.body: The improving / stable / declining arrows next to each dimension name now carry aria-labels and tooltips so the trend is announced to screen readers and visible on hover, not only via the legend.

items.headline: Duplicate freshness marker removed
items.body: Each dimension card showed both a 'Last reviewed' pill on the card face and an 'Updated YYYY-MM-DD' line above Key Metrics. The pill is now the single canonical freshness marker.

items.headline: Grade-change marker is now within the readable font floor
items.body: The '(was X)' previous-grade marker bumped from 11px to 12px so the mobile font-size floor catches it; the design tokens disallow body text below 12px.

summary: Mobile disclosure placement fix: headline-score and approval drill-downs now open directly under the tapped card on phones.

items.headline: Score math opens where mobile readers expect it
items.body: On narrow screens, the Household Impact and Full Policy Audit derivation panels now render immediately below the card that opened them instead of after all four headline boxes.

items.headline: Approval details follow the same mobile pattern
items.body: The Approval Signal drill-down now uses the same responsive ordering, so tapping the card scrolls to the poll details directly under that card on phones.

summary: Internal traceability pass: triggers whose evidence lives inside the dashboard now jump to their evidence home instead of remaining grey labels.

items.headline: Internal evidence homes are now clickable
items.body: Major Projects triggers can jump to the project pipeline, Flagship Delivery triggers can jump back to the home-dimension grid, and Promise Delivery triggers can open the Promises tab.

items.headline: Defence & Trade split tripwire tightened
items.body: The split rule now covers both opposite movement and widening sub-score gaps, and it explicitly uses two consecutive monthly review cycles as the promotion test.

items.headline: Ethics trigger language made more concrete
items.body: The governance-critique down-trigger now names the threshold directly: two or more listed governance sources must publish a material disclosure or screening gap finding.

items.headline: Promise Delivery stays visibly tracker-only
items.body: The expanded tracker card now shows its own trigger traceability without using grade language, and stale copy about future GPA removal was replaced with current tracker-only wording.

summary: Traceability cleanup follow-on: the audit now matches the live model, Defence & Trade carries an explicit split tripwire, and several easy trigger links were filled in.

items.headline: Consistency audit corrected to match the live tracker / scoring split
items.body: The new consistency self-audit no longer describes Promise Delivery as a live graded file. It now treats Promise Delivery as what the product already is: a derivative accountability tracker that sits outside the 11 performance grades.

items.headline: Defence & Trade now carries a visible split-promotion rule
items.body: The file still stays combined for now, but the methodology now says what breaks that structure: if the defence and trade sub-scores move in opposite directions for two consecutive review cycles, the split shadow promotes into live separate files.

items.headline: Another batch of trigger links was threaded
items.body: Climate, immigration, and housing now carry a few more direct trigger-source links where the public source home already existed, reducing the number of move conditions that still rely on label-only references.

items.headline: Promise Delivery no longer carries a live-grade field in current data
items.body: The tracker still keeps its internal accountability logic, but the live dimension data no longer exposes Promise Delivery as if it were a peer A–F score inside the current board.

summary: Traceability pass: grade-change triggers now carry their own source labels, exception files are framed more honestly, and source stacks are rebalanced into a tighter band.

items.headline: One-notch grade triggers now point at their own source homes
items.body: Move-up and move-down conditions are no longer just free-floating editorial text. Each trigger now carries its own source label, and where a public document exists, a direct source link appears immediately underneath it in the scoring drawer.

items.headline: Readers no longer have to infer which source backs which trigger
items.body: Expanded dimension cards now render a small source line under every one-notch trigger. That means the chain from grade to move condition to supporting source is shorter and more explicit than before.

items.headline: Thin and overloaded source stacks were rebalanced
items.body: Affordability Response, Housing Supply, and Promise Delivery now carry stronger public source trails, while Economic Policy Response was thinned back from a kitchen-sink stack to the same tighter 5-8 source band used elsewhere on the dashboard.

items.headline: Exception files are framed more honestly
items.body: Defence & Trade now explains why it remains one mixed file, and Flagship Delivery now identifies itself more clearly as a derived rollup instead of reading like a normal home dimension.

summary: Trust-feedback pass: the scorecard now explains what it is and is not for, makes freshness harder to miss, and shows where judgment enters each grade.

items.headline: Scorecard framing made explicit
items.body: The Scorecard view now opens with a compact plain-language note: this is a public performance scorecard built from thresholds, source links, and review dates; it is not a forecast, voting guide, popularity measure, or claim that only measurable files matter.

items.headline: Freshness is more visible
items.body: The header now treats the global Updated date as a visible badge, and each dimension's Last reviewed date is styled as a stronger review marker instead of a quiet italic footer.

items.headline: Judgment calls surfaced on every graded card
items.body: Each graded dimension now has a short card-face Judgment call line and a longer Where judgment enters explanation in the scoring drawer, so readers can separate source evidence, thresholds, and editor judgment.

items.headline: Mobile trust surfaces tightened
items.body: On narrow screens, the Scorecard framing now renders as a compact visible panel, Last reviewed pills use stronger contrast, and the Promises tab summary wraps cleanly so statuses like Abandoned are not clipped.

summary: Mobile scoreboard drill-downs now scroll into view, methodology shorthand was removed from the card surface, and the visitor counter is visible again with a same-origin fallback that no longer overlaps the mobile header.

items.headline: Visitor counter restored with a mobile-safe placement
items.body: The sitewide visitor count is back with a same-origin fallback, so browsers that block third-party analytics requests still show a real number instead of a missing badge. On phones, the badge now drops into normal flow above the title instead of floating over it.

items.headline: Headline-score panels now come into view on mobile
items.body: Tapping Household Impact, Full Policy Audit, or Approval Signal on a phone no longer leaves the opened detail panel far below the scoreboard strip. The dashboard now scrolls the panel into view automatically.

items.headline: Internal shorthand pills removed from dimension cards
items.body: Surface labels like "Credit-claiming penalty," "Sub-score file," and "Long-lag file" were removed from the card face. The underlying scoring logic still exists, but it now lives in the expanded explanation instead of reading like internal shorthand on the surface.

items.headline: Scoring adjustments rewritten in plainer language
items.body: Expanded card explanations now use reader-facing labels such as "External pressure," "Early-cycle adjustment," and "Credit reduced for overclaiming" instead of internal modifier names.

summary: Inspectability pass: headline scores now show their math, Major Projects is graded on cohort progress, and the scoring drawer carries a confidence / attribution / lag glossary.

items.headline: Headline scores now show how they're built
items.body: Both the Household Impact and Full Policy Audit cards have a new "How is this score built?" toggle. Click it and the dashboard shows the per-dimension grade, the points, the weight, and the arithmetic that produces the headline letter — so any reader can verify the score against the cards.

items.headline: Major Projects regraded on cohort progress, not first-event triggers
items.body: The Major Projects rubric now defines the project universe (16 projects across 3 MPO tranches as of April 2026) and grades on documented post-designation movement, not just promoted stage labels. The dimension card carries the full project list with each project's current stage and source link. As of 2026-04-30, 4 projects sit above designated status, but only 2 of 16 (~13%) show later-dated post-designation advancement in the recorded cohort data — which keeps the file at C.

items.headline: Confidence / Attribution / Lag glossary inside the scoring drawer
items.body: The three small pills at the top of every dimension's scoring drawer now sit above a one-click "What do these mean?" definition box: a one-sentence explanation each for confidence, attribution, and lag, with the level cutoffs spelled out (High / Medium / Low; Direct / Mixed / Mostly inherited; Short / Medium / Long / Event-driven).

summary: Methodology hardening pass: all dimensions now surface scoring logic, threshold language tightened, and Economic Policy / Ethics source gaps narrowed.

items.headline: Scoring drawers expanded across the dashboard
items.body: Every dimension now exposes its construct, threshold ladder, move triggers, and guardrails inside the card, instead of limiting that transparency to only three audited files.

items.headline: Threshold language tightened across the rubric
items.body: The rubric and canonical scoring sheets were rewritten to use more explicit counts, ranges, and decision rules, with less reliance on words like “credible,” “substantive,” or “material” standing alone.

items.headline: Economic Policy now tracks non-spending levers explicitly
items.body: The live file now surfaces business investment, tax competitiveness, internal-trade execution, regulatory-burden work, and permitting-adjacent checks alongside AI and critical-minerals funding.

items.headline: Ethics challenge stack broadened
items.body: Ethics & Transparency now includes the House ETHI report on the Conflict of Interest Act alongside Democracy Watch and official commissioner materials, reducing dependence on a single advocacy voice.

summary: Majority government confirmed, climate grade moved down to D, new public-approval signal at the top, and a readability pass across the dashboard.

items.headline: Climate & Environment moved D+ → D
items.body: Canada is tracking for about half of its required 2030 emissions reduction. Industrial carbon credits are trading near $20/t despite a $95 headline. ECCC is losing 840+ positions. The PM has acknowledged targets will be missed.
drivers: Industrial credits detached from headline price

items.headline: Majority government confirmed
items.body: Carney's Liberals won 3 Toronto/Quebec byelections on April 13, 2026, reaching 174 seats and securing a majority in the House of Commons.

items.headline: Federal gas tax suspension announced
items.body: Federal fuel excise suspended April 20 through September 7, 2026. Estimated $2.4B in foregone revenue over the window.

items.headline: Approval Signal added to the top of the dashboard
items.body: 60-day rolling average of approve/disapprove across five included pollsters (Léger, Abacus, Ipsos, Angus Reid Institute, Innovative Research). Tracked beside the grades but explicitly not one of them — popularity is not performance.

items.headline: Readability pass on the dashboard
items.body: Plainer card labels, shorter status lines, a new "Limits of this model" note in the Rubric tab, a per-dimension "Last reviewed" line, and an across-the-board font-size bump for mobile.

summary: Climate grade revision (since rolled forward), source stack broadened, probation dimensions normalized to whole-letter C.

items.headline: Source stack expanded
items.body: Added Canadian Climate Institute, IFSD, IRPP / Policy Options, La Presse, Toronto Star, National Observer, and The Conversation Canada to the graded dimensions.

items.headline: Probation dimensions normalized to whole-letter C
items.body: Ethics & Transparency and Flagship Delivery now score as whole letters only (no plus/minus precision behind the displayed grade).
